statements.status_notes: PingAuthorize Server is not vulnerable to this CVE related to Java serialization because it does not use Spring's HttpInvoker endpoints. Additionally, the CVE mentions vulnerable versions all through 5.3.16, and PingAuthorize 10.2 is using Spring 5.3.39 which is not affected by it.
PingAuthorize includes guava 33 which is not vulnerable to this CVE.

Apache has rated this issue as a medium https://camel.apache.org/security/CVE-2020-11971.html This issue only affects customers, who are actively using the Camel service module in their Policies, see https://docs.pingidentity.com/r/en-us/pingauthorize-92/paz_camel_services to determine if that's the case. This module will be deprecated in the version 9.3 of PingAuthorize.

PingAuthorize utilizes Velocity Engine 2.4.1 to render templates through Velocity HTTP Servlet Extension. Velocity 1.6.2 is included for compatibility support with PingDataMetrics https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingdirectory/9.2/pingdatametrics_server_administration_guide/pd_met_velocity_tools_context_prov.html. It will be upgraded to 1.7.1 in the upcoming release (June 30th). This version includes a fix for CVE-2020-13936. Eventually this jar will be removed.
This CVE pertains to org.apache.httpcomponents:httpclient versions 4.5.12 or lower. PingAuthorize uses version 4.5.13. commons-httpclient is a different library and is not affected by this CVE.

PingAuthorize does not utilize velocity-tools as a renderer hence the CVE is not exploiable. The feature it is used for is deprecated and will be removed in future releases https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingdirectory/9.3/pingdatametrics_server_administration_guide/pd_met_velocity_tools_context_prov.html
The Bouncy Castle component will be upgraded to version 1.0.2.5 in version 10.3 of the product. This library is optional and only used when the product is setup in the FIPS compliant mode.

There are no confirmations from the Swagger team that DOMPurify CVEs can be exploited. The Swagger web application does all its processing in the browser; it does not store any data. Hence, I don’t see how an attacker is able to deliver XSS payloads. The swagger-ui HTTP Servlet extension can be safely removed, if not needed by executing a command `dsconfig delete-http-servlet-extension --extension-name "Swagger UI"`
PingAuthorize does not use the vulnerable function named in CVE-2021-23463 and is not vulnerable to this issue.

PingAuthorize is not vulnerable to this issue found in our custom csd (collect support data) tool because of how Ping manages dependency downloads. This CVE is related to insecure (http, as opposed to https) calls to maven central during development or runtime that could potentially create a supply chain vulnerability if the dependency being requested has been spoofed or compromised. PingAuthorize is not vulnerable to this because our dependency calls go to internal Ping sources, not out to maven central. csd will never make a call out to maven central for a dependency on its own.

Multiple git submodules are present in the PingAuthorize image’s Alpine OS. As these are written in golang, the packages contain go files as dependencies, however, no go commands are executable on PingAuthorize, meaning that even with local access to a container, vulnerabilities in go language components cannot be exploited. If the case arises that a vulnerability in go can be exploited in an Alpine package, we would act on and patch it accordingly.

This vulnerability relies on creating a file larger than 1 GB of data in C:\etc\os-release or C:\usr\lib\os-release on a windows environment before the start of the application in order to cause resource exhaustion and crash the application. Ensure these files don't exist or are small enough that they will not overload the JVM memory size (the default JVM maximum memory size is set to 1 GB). Jakarta is used by PingAuthorize for sending status notification and alerts https://docs.pingidentity.com/pingdirectory/10.3/pingdirectory_server_administration_guide/pd_ds_manage_notifs_alerts.html. To successfully exploit the vulnerability, the server needs to send an email with content-type header set to `text/html;charset=utf-8`  mentioned in https://gitlab.eclipse.org/security/vulnerability-reports/-/issues/290. This is not possible in PingAuthorize, as the type is hardcoded to text/plain; charset=us-ascii. To prevent the CVE from appearing in future scans, the dependency will be upgraded to version 2.0.2 in version 11 of the product.

The reported Golang vulnerabilities originate from operating-system–level packages (for example, git-lfs) present in the PingAuthorize container’s Alpine base image, not from PingAuthorize itself. Although these packages are implemented in Golang and therefore include Go standard libraries, PingAuthorize does not ship, invoke, or depend on any Go-based binaries or libraries as part of its runtime. There is no execution path by which PingAuthorize can trigger or leverage Golang components: 1. PingAuthorize is a Java-based application; 2. The affected Go binaries are not called by PingAuthorize during normal operation; 3. Exploitation would require direct execution of the OS-level binary, which is outside the PingAuthorize threat model and unrelated to product functionality. If a Golang vulnerability were to be identified that is exploitable through an OS-level package independently of PingAuthorize, remediation would be handled via base image or operating system updates, not via PingAuthorize code or configuration changes. This applies to all mentioned Go CVEs: CVE-2025-47914, CVE-2025-58181, CVE-2025-68121, CVE-2025-58183, CVE-2025-61726, CVE-2025-61728, CVE-2025-22873, CVE-2025-47906, CVE-2025-47912, CVE-2025-58185, CVE-2025-58186, CVE-2025-58189, CVE-2025-61724, CVE-2025-61727, CVE-2025-61730, CVE-2026-27139, CVE-2026-25679, CVE-2026-27142

This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console because its default resource locations are not filesystem-based. Spring framework dependencies are scheduled to be updated in version 11.2 of the product.

This CVE is not exploitable within Admin Console instances deployed on the embedded PingDirectory / PingAuthorize Jetty server, as Jetty automatically performs URI normalization and validation. Spring framework dependencies are scheduled to be updated in version 11.2 of the product.

The Admin Console application does not use JSP (JavaServer Pages); therefore, this vulnerability is not exploitable.

This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console because the application does not evaluate user-supplied SpEL expressions.

While the vulnerability is theoretically exploitable, it requires highly privileged access, as only administrators are permitted to create SpEL definitions. The affected component will be upgraded in the upcoming 2026.Q3 release.
This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console because the application does not evaluate user-supplied SpEL expressions.

This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console because the application does not accept or process multipart requests; therefore, the core prerequisites for this smuggling vector are not met. Spring framework dependencies are scheduled to be updated in version 11.2 of the product.
This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console as it does not invoke UriComponentsBuilder methods using user-controlled URIs.

Netty is a transitive dependency of the Azure SDK. Internal path analysis confirms the vulnerable code path is only reachable via the Azure Key Vault passphrase provider component. Due to the high complexity required to influence the DNS resolution chain within this specific operational context, exploitability is considered unlikely in a real-world scenario. The Azure SDK is scheduled to be updated in the upcoming 2026.Q3 release.

The vulnerability is theoretically exploitable through the Azure Key Vault passphrase provider; however, a successful attack requires the threat actor to control an authoritative nameserver for a registered subdomain under the target domain/TLD. The Azure SDK will be updated to a patched version in the upcoming 2026.Q3 release.

The vulnerability is theoretically exploitable through the Azure Key Vault passphrase provider; however, a successful attack requires the threat actor to control an authoritative nameserver for a registered subdomain under the target domain/TLD. The Azure SDK will be updated to a patched version in the upcoming 2026.Q3 release.

This CVE is not exploitable within the Admin Console because the application does not enable X.509 principal extraction; therefore, the required technical prerequisites are not met. The underlying Spring Framework dependencies are scheduled to be updated in version 11.2 of the product.

The /usr/local/bin/vault binary is not included in the standard distribution of PingAuthorize and was likely introduced solely during the initial container deployment lifecycle. The product codebase does not invoke this tool at runtime, and there is no vector for a remote attacker to trigger execution. Therefore, these CVEs are not exploitable within the application.

The /usr/local/bin/vault binary is not included in the standard distribution of PingAuthorize and was likely introduced solely during the initial container deployment lifecycle. The product codebase does not invoke this tool at runtime, and there is no vector for a remote attacker to trigger execution. Therefore, these CVEs are not exploitable within the application.

PingAuthorize is not vulnerable to this issue. The product does not use enableDefaultTyping() or BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator - polymorphic deserialization is entirely absent from our ObjectMapperFactory implementation. Jackson library is scheduled for an upgrade for the Q3 release.

PingAuthorize is not vulnerable to this issue. ACCEPT_CASE_INSENSITIVE_PROPERTIES is never enabled. The configuration call within ObjectMapperFactory is a no-op due to a discarded builder result, meaning the feature remains inactive and cannot be exploited. Jackson library is scheduled for an upgrade for the Q3 release.

The CVE requires the application to actively call MapMessage.asJson() or use JsonTemplateLayout; neither is present in PingData Admin Console. Furthermore, this component is entirely optional and can be safely disabled if required.

This CVE affects OpenTelemetry's baggage propagation parser. PingAuthorize OpenTelemetry integration configures only W3C trace context propagation (traceparent/tracestate headers). Baggage propagation is never registered or invoked. The vulnerable code path cannot be reached. The component is scheduled for an upgrade for the Q3 release.

This CVE is not exploitable in PingAuthorize. It requires a specific annotation pattern in Java model classes: a getter method annotated with @JsonProperty paired with a setter annotated with @JsonIgnore on the same field. A review of all Jackson-annotated model classes in this codebase confirms that pattern is not present. Jackson library is scheduled for an upgrade for the Q3 release.

This CVE is not exploitable in PingAuthorize. It requires the application to use Jackson's @JsonView annotation to restrict which properties are included during deserialization. The feature is never configured, the vulnerable code path in BeanDeserializer cannot be reached. Jackson library is scheduled for an upgrade for the Q3 release.

According to the advisory https://github.com/netty/netty/security/advisories/GHSA-g7hg-vrcf-mvmr, this vulnerability affects only `netty-handler-ssl-ocsp` component. This component is not included by PingAuthorize hence the product is not vulnerable.

This vulnerability is not exploitable within PingAuthorize, as the product does not utilize the vulnerable SPDY classes. Additionally, the underlying Netty component is scheduled for an upgrade in the upcoming 11.2 major release.

This vulnerability is not exploitable, as DelegatingDecompressorFrameListener is not utilized by the product. Additionally, the underlying Netty component is scheduled for an upgrade in the upcoming 11.2 major release.

This vulnerability is not exploitable within PingAuthorize, as the product does not utilize the vulnerable SPDY classes. Additionally, the underlying Netty component is scheduled for an upgrade in the upcoming 11.2 major release.
PingAuthorize does not utilize Netty's CorsHandler; therefore, this vulnerability is not exploitable within the product.

This CVE is not exploitable, as PingAuthorize does not utilize the 100-Continue logic required to trigger the vulnerability. Additionally, Jetty was upgraded to a non-vulnerable version in PingAuthorize 11.1.

False positive: PingAuthorize does not utilize JMS components, rendering this finding non-exploitable. Additionally, PingAuthorize 11.1 updates the Spring Framework to a patched, non-vulnerable release.

PingAuthorize uses Bouncy Castle only for password hashing primitives (Argon2, BCrypt, SCrypt) and as a FIPS/JSSE security provider for TLS. The OCSP revocation checker is never invoked. There is no OCSP stapling validation path through Bouncy Castle anywhere in the codebase.
The product does not utilize hostname verification via BCJSSE; therefore, this CVE is not exploitable.

This CVE is in Bouncy Castle's DHAgreement class, which performs static DH key agreement without validating the peer's public value. PingAuthorize does not use Bouncy Castle's DH key exchange. Bouncy Castle is used only for password hashing primitives (Argon2, BCrypt, SCrypt) and optionally as a FIPS crypto provider. The vulnerable DHAgreement code path is never invoked.
In the default (non-FIPS) configuration, the JDK's built-in PKIX trust manager handles certificate validation and name constraints; Bouncy Castle is not in that path.
BKS and UBER - the two types backed by the vulnerable BcKeyStoreSpi - are never used. Not exploitable.
The vulnerable KCCMBlockCipher code path is never invoked. Not exploitable.
PingAuthorize does not use any Bouncy Castle encryption engines or IES primitives. The vulnerable IESEngine code path is never invoked. Not exploitable.
The vulnerable bcprov RSADigestSigner is never invoked by the product. Not exploitable.

bc-fips is only loaded when FIPS mode is explicitly enabled; in non-FIPS deployments, the library is never placed on the classpath. Customers requiring a mitigation can manually replace the bc-fips library with a newer version. No code or configuration changes are required. The shipped library version will be upgraded in PingAuthorize 11.2.
This CVE is in Bouncy Castle's LazyEncodedSequence and ASN1InputStream - triggered when parsing deeply nested ASN.1 structures. The product does not use Bouncy Castle's ASN.1 parser. Not exploitable.
This CVE is in Bouncy Castle's LazyEncodedSequence and ASN1InputStream - triggered when parsing deeply nested ASN.1 structures. The product does not use Bouncy Castle's ASN.1 parser. Not exploitable.

This CVE affects only the asynchronous (non-blocking) JSON parser in NonBlockingUtf8JsonParserBase. The async parser is never used in the codebase.The vulnerable code path cannot be reached. Not exploitable.
The SPDY protocol is never configured or used anywhere in the codebase. The vulnerable decoder cannot be reached. Not exploitable.
No org.bouncycastle.asn1 classes are used anywhere in the product or LDAP SDK source. Not exploitable.
No org.bouncycastle.pqc or HSS/LMS classes are used anywhere in the codebase. Not exploitable.

Not affected: PAZ's Redis usage is strictly limited to simple key-value operations (getBucket().get(), setAsync(), pingAll()) and contains no Lua scripts. Since Lua execution is a prerequisite for this CVE, the vulnerability cannot be exploited.

This CVE affects PingAuthorize only when running in FIPS-compliant mode using bc-fips 2.x on Intel x86/x86-64 hardware. Deployments utilizing FIPS 140-2 mode (bc-fips 1.0.x) or operating on non-Intel architectures are not affected. Customers requiring immediate mitigation can manually replace the bc-fips library with an updated version. No additional code or configuration changes are required. The bundled library will be officially upgraded in the PingAuthorize 11.2 release.
Apache Thrift is not a dependency of PingAuthorize or any related products. Consequently, this finding has been determined to be a false positive.
The product does not use any Bouncy Castle block cipher or AEAD modes. BC usage is limited to password hashing primitives and optionally the FIPS provider.
The product does not use DTLS; therefore, this CVE is not exploitable.

The product's CryptoHelper explicitly restricts supported keystore types to JKS, PKCS12, BCFKS, and PKCS11. The BKS (and UBER) keystore types are never used. There is no API surface for a user to configure or present a BKS keystore to the product. The vulnerable code path cannot be reached.
This CVE is not exploitable in PingAuthorize, as Bzip2Decoder is never instantiated or wired into any processing pipeline. Netty will be upgraded in PingAuthorize 11.2.

Exploitation requires using jackson-core's non-blocking API. There is no usage of NonBlockingJsonParser, createNonBlockingByteArrayParser, or AsyncInputFeeder anywhere in the product source. The product uses only the standard synchronous parser. Jackson will be upgraded in version 11.2 of the product

The affected component is used by the PingData Administrative Console. However, the Admin Console does not accept or inject external configuration that enables LoggingMeterRegistry or a StatsD registry, which are required prerequisites for exploitation. Therefore, this CVE is not exploitable.

This CVE is not exploitable in the context of PingAuthorize, as none of the vulnerable classes are utilized by the product: DnsNameResolver, DnsResolver, DefaultDnsRecordDecoder, DnsCodecUtil, DnsRecord, and Netty DNS decoder classes.

The product does not use Reactor Netty to implement an HTTP server. The vulnerable HTTP/1.1 pipelining code path is therefore not reachable by external requests, and the CVE is not exploitable in the product.
The product does not use the vulnerable Flux.windowTimeout operator or enable fairBackpressure. Therefore, the CVE is not exploitable in the product.
The product does not use the vulnerable Flux.bufferTimeout operator or enable fairBackpressure. Therefore, the CVE is not exploitable in the product.
The product does not utilize the XsltView class, XSLT view resolver, XSLT configuration, or XSLT templates. Therefore, the CVE is not exploitable.

The product does not utilize SimpleEvaluationContext, compiled-SpEL configuration, SpelParserConfiguration, or spring.expression.compiler.mode. Therefore, this CVE is not exploitable. The Spring Framework dependency will be updated in PingAuthorize 11.2.

Customers running customer-managed PingAuthorize deployments will need to upgrade their underlying Oracle JVM instances directly once the patch is available.

Not affected. CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Node.js built-in Brotli decoder, exploitable only where a Node.js runtime decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data. PingAuthorize does not ship or execute a Node.js runtime: the Node.js-built UI is compiled ahead of time into static JavaScript bundles served by the product, and at request time the browser (not Node.js) renders it and performs any Content-Encoding decompression using the browser's own Brotli implementation, which is separate code and not affected by this CVE. Node.js is used only in CI build containers, which are not deployed to production.

PingAuthorize is generally not vulnerable to the CVEs related to Apache Camel. Camel services are disabled by default and have been removed from the default configuration since PingAuthorize versions 10.2 and 10.3.

Customers who still depend on them are recommended to use a specific Camel version, 3.22.x and then 4.11.0. These versions are included as a bridge for customers with existing policies that use Camel. The vulnerable camel-http is shipped only for them.
